newsitem.title: USA: SanDisk wins patent suit against Samsung.
newsitem.headline: SanDisk wins patent suit against Samsung.

text.p: SanDisk Corp said late Wednesday that a U.S. International Trade Commission judge has ruled that Samsung Electronics Co and Samsung Semiconductor Inc are infringing two SanDisk U.S. patents involving flash memory.

SanDisk said remedies for the violations may include an order prohibiting Samsung from further importing the products, a cease and desist order prohibiting the sales of imported Samsung flash memory devices, or both.

SanDisk, a flash data storage products supplier based in Sunnyvale, California, said Administrative Law Judge Sidney Harris issued the ruling and that the full commission is expected to act on the recommendation within 90 days.
The company filed its complaint in January, 1996.
Neither company could be immediately reached for comment.

"Although the ITC has yet to act on the judge's determination, SanDisk believes that this ruling is a positive first step in vindicating SanDisk's intellectual property rights in its flash memory technology and is hopeful the commission will affirm the judge's ruling," the company said in a release.
